about: The live rule monitor's pre-registration (scripts/rule_monitor.py), 2026-10-21. One test for every rule that bets: the Predictions pick rules and segments (scripts/games_picks.py) and the paper book rules (scripts/paper_book.py, whose kill switch was the window test alone: it now adds the CUSUM, which catches a rule that turns after a good run about twice as fast). A rule stops when, with minN+ bets judged by the close since its clock started, either its last `window` are worth clustered t below `t` at the close (game day as the cluster), or a one-sided CUSUM on close value standardised by the rule's backtest sd crosses h. It comes back only when it is refit (a pick rule's X or k changes, or a refit re-tests it; a paper rule is changed), which restarts its clock.

cusum.note: S = max(0, S - z - k) per bet in kick order, z = clvRet / sd. k .25, h 10, picked on simulation (sd .12, 4 bets a game day, checked every game day, 600 bets) with the paper book's old window test (last 300, t < -1) kept beside it: a rule losing 1.5% a bet to the close stops by a median 60 bets, losing 3% by 52; one that turns from +3% to -3% after 200 bets stops ~104 bets after the turn (the window test alone: 200); one really at +1.5% stops 6% of the time, at +3% 3%, at the close about two in three (it loses the vig anyway)
